headline: 🔥 A LISTING THAT HAD PRODUCED NOTHING FOR A MONTH JUST HANDED YOU THE BEST SIGNAL ON THE BOARD — 821 Martinwood was shown twice this weekend and the agent's Saturday buyer came back "VERY interested," and the same two emails prove the price cut you approved seventeen days ago DID take effect. ⚡ DO: call the Fieldstone sellers — an inspector has their door code Thursday and it is now two days unsaid. ⚠️ WATCH: the 198 Rena listing agreement dies Friday, day five unruled.

notes: ✅ FIXED TONIGHT — THE PUBLISH LANE IS OPEN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN SEVEN DAYS. The GitHub CLI was signed in at 8:11 PM and all NINETEEN stranded commits shipped; this board is the first thing your phone has shown since Tuesday morning. ⭐ THE CAUSE, CONFIRMED: your GitHub token lived in Windows Credential Manager, which is encrypted per-user and Windows-only — it was never a file, so the Mac migration could not carry it. The Keychain, gh, ~/.git-credentials and ~/.ssh were all empty, so git fell back to prompting for a username and a scheduled run has no terminal to answer with. That is why it failed sixteen times identically instead of intermittently. Verified fixed for unattended runs — a non-interactive credential lookup now returns a live token.

🔴 THE CEO SWEEP LANDED AT 5:15 AND FOUND FOUR ROUTINES THAT DIED SILENTLY. Its new silent-run check compares what the scheduler says ran against what actually wrote a heartbeat — and the nightly Deep Dive, your highest-earning routine, STARTED and produced nothing on three consecutive nights (8/6, 8/7, 8/8). The old check could not tell that apart from a quiet night, which is why three of them passed unflagged. Money Machine, the trading cockpit and the Saturday spot are the other three.

✅ EVERYTHING ELSE RAN A CORRECTLY QUIET SUNDAY. The ISA sweep returned true zeros on every instrument all day under your no-touch rule and still caught four net-new leads for Monday's 7 AM queue; the milestone engine scanned twenty-nine listings across four passes and fired nothing; the Delta's afternoon pass went out silent because none of its five material triggers cleared. Quiet by rule, not quiet by failure.

callBlock.why: 🆕 THE NEWEST AND CLEANEST SIGNAL ON THE WHOLE BOARD, four hours old. She showed 821 Martinwood to two different buyers this weekend and filed both feedback forms ninety seconds apart Sunday afternoon: Saturday's buyer is "VERY interested," Sunday's is not. ⛔ EVERY OTHER FIELD ON BOTH FORMS IS BLANK — no price opinion, no comments, no recommendation. She has told you someone wants the house and nothing at all about why, which is exactly what a phone call is for. ⭐ It is also the first written read this listing has produced in the entire fourteen-day window. Ask what her Saturday buyer liked, what is holding them, and what gets them in — your seller is motivated. Never name a price concession.

⏰ NOW A BEFORE-MONDAY-1:40 CALL. She wrote the 7/25 offer on 355 Comanche, answered interested YES, called the old $299,000 too high — and still does not know the price came down to $295,000. Yesterday's 1:30 showing came and went while she was uninformed; the next appointment lands Monday at 1:40. That is two showings' worth of missed timing on the one fact that answers her only objection.

callBlock.who: Angela B. (buyer's agent, Keller Williams Vestavia)
callBlock.why: ⭐ THE OTHER 'INTERESTED: YES' ON THE SAME LISTING, and the same story — her only objection was price, and the price has since been answered. Her free text said her buyer saw another home she likes, which is a cross-shopping buyer rather than a rejection. ⏳ This read ages out of the fourteen-day window Friday, so the call has a shelf life.

SHE ASKED FOR A PROFESSIONAL VALUATION IN HER OWN WORDS on 145 Detroit Ave — a seller raising her hand, not a lead to qualify. ✅ Her first-touch email went out Saturday by your own cold-send rule. The follow-through is a call, and it has been sitting since Friday.

🔴 STILL THE WORST NUMBER ON THIS LIST: ZERO TOUCHES OF ANY KIND, EVER, and now six days overdue. Third buyer off your 1709 Fieldstone ad, and he re-engaged himself on a Sunday afternoon. ⭐ The ad that produced him went under contract Saturday, so the property he called about is gone and he does not know it — which is a reason to call, not a reason not to.

THE FIRST AND ONLY REPLY THE RECONNECT LANE HAS EVER PRODUCED, now seven days old — and he has since become both sides of a deal: he wants something inexpensive on Lay or Logan Martin, you sent him the Highland Crest valuation, and you are running his mortgage numbers. Three revenue lines in one relationship and no call yet.

Fourth name off the 1709 Fieldstone ad in four days, landed 7:47 PM on a Sunday while the instant responder was dark. ⭐ Same point as Anthony M. — the ad that produced her just went under contract, so she is a live buyer whose target is off the market and who has heard nothing from you either way.

387 Appleford Rd in Helena with roughly $202K in equity, dark since September 2025. ⭐ Equity plus silence is the classic listing conversation — she is not waiting on you, which is exactly why the call has to originate from your side.

listings.status: 🔍 UNDER CONTRACT $390K → INSPECTION Thursday 8/13 at 11:15 AM — and TWO DAYS on, the sellers still have not been told
listings.note: 🔑 THIS IS THE CALL, AND IT HAS NOW SLIPPED A SECOND DAY. An inspector has your sellers' lockbox combo for Thursday at 11:15, you set that time yourself Saturday evening, and a sweep of both your aliases still finds nothing outbound to them. The 9:30 block passed this morning, the 5 PM window has passed now. ⭐ It is a two-minute call with nothing but good news in it — their house is under contract at $390,000 and the inspection is locked.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $295K — yesterday's 1:30 held with no read yet, and the next one lands Monday 1:40
listings.note: ⏳ THE TEST IS HALF RUN AND THE ANSWER HASN'T ARRIVED. The 1:30 went ahead Sunday — the first traffic since the competing offer was confirmed dead — and no written read has come off it in the four hours since. Monday's 1:40 is still on the books. 🔴 BOTH NAMED 'INTERESTED: YES' AGENTS STILL DO NOT KNOW THE PRICE CAME DOWN, and that is now two showings' worth of missed timing rather than one. Both calls are Monday-morning calls, before the 1:40.

listings.status: ⚠️ Under contract $351K — the appraisal ran Friday morning and 46 hours later no value exists anywhere
listings.note: ⚠️ THE APPRAISAL IS THE STORY, NOT THE REPAIR COUNTER. It ran Friday at 9:00 AM and no value has reported in any lane in about forty-six hours. That is drifting out of comfortable and it is the single number this entire file turns on. ⏰ THE REPAIR ADDENDUM HAS NOW SAT UNANSWERED ON DOTLOOP SINCE FRIDAY 6:35 PM — roughly thirty-seven hours — over a gap of three hundred dollars on a $351,000 contract, with the seller handling HVAC and the other side already saying they will get it signed. Still the cheapest decision on your board, and it is getting more expensive to have left it. ⚠️ Older paper is unsigned too, on a file where the closing agent already holds the earnest money, and the buyers' own home-sale contingency has never been receipted. ⭐ For the seller conversation: contract price is $351,000, not the $369,000 list — every repair dollar comes off a net that already carries $8,000 in closing costs and a warranty.

listings.status: 🔴 Active $450K — DAY FIVE UNRULED, your listing agreement dies Friday, and Sunday's showing cancelled
listings.note: 🔴 STILL THE HARDEST DEADLINE ON YOUR BOARD AND THE ONLY ONE NOBODY IS TOUCHING. The agreement expires Friday 8/14 while the counter under discussion proposes a contingency deadline past your authority to represent these sellers. 🆕 SUNDAY'S NEAR-MISS: a 4:30 showing was requested, confirmed and cancelled inside 100 minutes — ⭐ for ILLNESS, not the house, confirmed and closed out by the ISA sweep at 2:37. Do not let that be read as market rejection in the agreement conversation. The seller call comes first; it is the same call that gets the agreement extended.

listings.status: 🎉 The listing appointment HELD Saturday — and they replied warm the same afternoon
listings.note: 🎉 THE WEEKEND'S OTHER REAL WIN, AND IT KEPT MOVING AFTER THE MEETING. You built the packet and forwarded it to both sellers sixteen minutes into the slot. ⭐ THEN THEY CAME BACK: the siding was completed October of 2021. That answers neither open question — no signature, no price — but it banks a dated capital improvement straight into the MLS input, and an unprompted reply hours after a listing appointment is exactly the tone you want. ⭐ THE BOARD ALSO EARNED A FACT IT HAD BEEN MISSING SINCE 7/20: the address and price band are known and a dossier exists for the first time. ⭐ It is a two-sided deal — they list this one and buy the next. ⚠️ Nothing is signed yet, which makes the follow-up the whole ballgame, and Monday is the day for it.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $899K — closing Thursday Aug 20, the extension IS signed, and your brokerage has the wrong date
listings.note: 🆕 CAUGHT AT MIDDAY: YOUR BROKERAGE'S SYSTEM THINKS THIS FUNDS FRIDAY. It does not — the re-issued closing invite reads Thursday Aug 20 at 3:00 PM at the law firm, and the earlier 'close 8/14' notice was a stale-date nag, verified and rejected rather than believed. Three clicks Monday morning fixes the record before anyone plans around a wrong week. ✅ THE ITEM THIS BOARD CARRIED AS OPEN FOR TWO DAYS IS CLOSED, AND THE BOARD HAD IT WRONG: the other side signed the extension addendum Saturday morning — the earlier reading of 'opened and not signed' came from an open-notice followed by a completion 43 seconds later that nobody read. Correction recorded rather than quietly dropped. ✅ THE DEAL IS OTHERWISE CLEAN: inspections done including septic, appraisal complete. ⚠️ ONE ITEM REMAINS AND IT IS YOURS: your brokerage's action-required request for the commission document — that is the paperwork that makes the payout happen, and it is on your call list. ⭐ Same seller as Altamont and Martinwood: three files, one phone call.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $164K — Friday evening's showing is now 42 hours old with no written read
listings.note: ⚠️ STILL THE ONE TO WATCH. A showing ran Friday at 6:00 PM and no read has filed in about forty-two hours — the oldest unanswered fresh tour on the board, on the listing holding the only unqualified 'interested YES, priced just right' this board has ever taken. ✅ YOU CLOSED THE AGENT CALL LATE FRIDAY NIGHT, five days after that yes landed. ⚠️ CLOSING THE CALL DID NOT MOVE THE BLOCKER, BECAUSE THE BLOCKER IS A DECISION: authorize a concession and trade a later close for a signed contract, or hold at list and let her buyer wait on a bonus that may or may not arrive. ⚠️ You still have not asked your seller for a number, and a decision with nothing behind it is theatre. ⏰ This file has also read AGREEMENT EXPIRING since 7/22 with no date ever pulled from the notice — eighteen days of an unread clock.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $559K — too high on the first read since the contract died, and five days quiet since
listings.note: ⚠️ THE FIRST TOUR AFTER A RE-LIST IS THE READ A PROPERTY GETS GRADED ON, and this one came back too high with the worst staging score on file. The two reads before the contract both said JUST RIGHT, so the shift is real and recent. 🔴 A HARDER QUESTION IS STILL OPEN: there is no bond on the EIFS here. On synthetic stucco a buyer's inspector finds that independently, and it is a plausible part of why a contract already died once. ⏰ NO NEW TOUR HAS BEEN BOOKED SINCE 8/4 — five days — and this file is down to two written reads in the window. ⭐ THE STAGING SCORE IS FIXABLE TODAY AND COSTS NOTHING. Fix that before anyone touches price.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $184K — two showings this weekend, a "VERY interested" buyer, and the price question finally settled
listings.note: 🔥 THE FILE TURNED OVER IN ONE AFTERNOON. This morning it read "twenty-eight days without a showing and no feedback history at all." Two ShowingTime emails at 4:33 and 4:35 PM replaced that with two weekend showings and the board's newest solid hit — Saturday's buyer came back VERY interested. ✅ AND THE SEVENTEEN-DAY PRICE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, THE GOOD WAY: both emails serve $184,000 ACTIVE straight off the MLS feed, so the cut you approved DID take effect. The two-public-prices risk is retired — what was actually wrong is that this board was carrying $189,000, and that is corrected here. ☎️ One call to the buyer's agent Monday. Same seller as Altamont and Lake Crest.

listings.status: 🔴 Active $364K — a read validated your price eleven days ago and the seller still has not been told
listings.note: 🔴 DAY ELEVEN OF A SELLER NOT HEARING GOOD NEWS, and the deadline is now inside a week: that read ages out of the fourteen-day window on Friday, at which point the only positive datapoint this listing has ever produced disappears off the board. A price called JUST RIGHT by someone with no reason to flatter it, overall rating 4 of 5, is exactly what an out-of-state condo seller wants to hear. ⚠️ A validated price with no buyer is a marketing conversation — and you cannot have it with someone who does not know the price was validated.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $1.15M — one tour in fourteen days, no written read, and the open house is nine days back
listings.note: ⚠️ YOUR MOST EXPENSIVE LISTING, SELLERS LIVING IN IT, exactly one booked tour in fourteen days and no written feedback at all. ⏰ Sunday's open house is nine days back and exists only in your head — well past the point where detail survives. Five minutes of dictation makes it usable; another week and it is gone. ✅ The marketing block on this listing cleared — the photo problem was a false alarm, all ten photos are live, and the carousel shipped. ⭐ THE LAND COMPONENT IS PINNED: the parcel runs 40 acres, and the one written objection this file has ever taken was about the land, not the price.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — she read your pre-list plan Thursday and the tenant answer is now seventeen days owed
listings.note: ⭐ SHE WAS BACK ON THE SITE 38 MINUTES AFTER YOUR PRE-LIST EMAIL — that is a seller reading her own plan and thinking about it, and it is the warmest this file has been in two weeks. 🔴 A CLIENT WHO HAS TO CHASE TWICE ON SOMETHING ORDINARY STARTS ASSUMING THE HARDER QUESTIONS WILL GO THE SAME WAY. Sixty seconds, whether or not you have the answer. ✅ The ceiling-height video she asked for has gone out, so the reason to call is concrete rather than apologetic. ⚠️ The condo scope email you promised 'shortly' is still owed.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active — cut $325K→$320K on 8/6 and the market has never been told
listings.note: ⚠️ A PRICE CUT NOBODY CAN SEE IS NOT A PRICE CUT. The reduction was made Wednesday and the announcement has sat unpublished ever since — three days of a listing carrying a stale public number while the seller believes it has been repriced. ⭐ Same failure shape as 821 Martinwood, and both are minutes to close. ⚠️ It was caught again in the marketing queue yesterday and re-contained, which means the guard is holding here even as it failed on Comanche.

listings.status: 🔴 Buyer-side $2.35M — the largest number on your board, and your written position still has not gone across
listings.note: 🔴 FIVE ASKS AND OVER TWO WEEKS OF SILENCE. Your own message told the other side you would entertain a reverse offer — a real position stated verbally with nothing on paper behind it. ⭐ The written feedback they have asked for five times IS your negotiating position; writing it is not a favour to them, it is putting your number on the record.

listings.status: 🔥 Cash deal — contract finalized and earnest money delivered; due diligence is the clock now
listings.note: 🔥 STILL THE FASTEST THING ON THIS BOARD BY A WIDE MARGIN — an offer-to-counter-to-counter round trip inside one day, and you confirmed the contract is finalized and earnest money delivered. ✅ THE ACREAGE BLOCKER IS RETIRED: the seller's own two numbers imply roughly 157.6 acres — the first acreage ever stated on this tract — so the deal can be valued. ⏰ THE DUE-DILIGENCE PACKAGE IS STAGED AND UNSTARTED, waiting on your word: a dated checklist with one line per item, because a DD period is a clock and a single task cannot show what is about to expire. ⚠️ A small conflict between two acreage figures remains on file; it changes the math at the margins, not the deal.

listings.client: ⚠️ seller verified, property still unnamed on the paperwork
listings.status: 🆕 A signed listing agreement that no system in the fleet can see — day seven
listings.note: 🆕 The signature is real and receipted; the parcel is not named anywhere in the document. ⚠️ Until it has an address it cannot be marketed, cannot be counted, and cannot be watched by any routine — it is inventory that exists only as a promise, and it is aging.

listings.addr: 19 Lots Deer Ridge Lakes · 2082 Narrows Point Cv · 118 Hayesbury Ln
listings.status: 🆕 COMING SOON — and two of them were supposed to go live THIS WEEKEND per your own note
listings.note: 🆕 YOU TOLD THE SYSTEM FRIDAY NIGHT THAT THE NARROWS LOT AND THE NINETEEN DEER RIDGE LOTS GO ON THE MARKET THIS WEEKEND — won inventory that nothing on this board was tracking as imminent, and the weekend is now here with no go-live receipt yet. ✅ They are recorded as COMING SOON rather than ACTIVE because the engine never demotes a status, so stamping them ACTIVE early would have been permanent. ⭐ They are visible to every routine instead of invisible, which is the point.

listings.status: 🎉 CLOSED AND PAID — and the feedback you owe the other agent is now openly overdue
listings.note: 🎉 ✅ PAID — ahead of what was modelled, which retires it from the stranded column entirely. ⚠️ WHAT DOES NOT RETIRE: the listing side asked for feedback three times and never got it, and their last ask is now eight days old. ⭐ The closing changed what that silence means — before it read as an oversight, now it reads as a shrug at the agent across the table on a deal you both just completed and both just got paid on. Their listing has since gone EXPIRED, so the window where your feedback is still useful to them is closing.

listings.status: 🎉 CLOSED 7/30 — day ten, and the money still has not reached the bank
listings.note: ⚠️ A closing with no receipted commission ten days later is the shape of a problem, not a delay — especially in a week where the business account has been the constraint every single day. ⭐ 683 Flag just proved these do land: that one was carried in this same column and paid Thursday, ahead of model.

listings.status: 🎉 CLOSED + FUNDED — one clean, one with a stranded payout
listings.note: ⚠️ WHISPERING PINES IS STILL STRANDED on an open agent-of-record question. ✅ THE HALF THAT WAS BLOCKING IT HAS MOVED: the teammate licence-compliance item was answered Thursday and both halves are done, so the administrative obstacle behind that question is cleared. Chase the payout itself now.

listings.status: 🆕 Buyer-side pending — the forecast found GCI nobody was counting
listings.note: ✅ Real money already on the board that had been missing from the count.

listings.status: 🛡️ Buyer-side — suppressed from the milestone engine, correctly
listings.note: ✅ The roster labelled you listing agent; four receipts say the other side holds the sellers. The guard went in before a wrong milestone could fire a seller email at someone who is not your seller.

listings.addr: 3035 County Line Rd · 104 95th St N · 361 White Oak Cir · 1230 Calvert Rd · 42770 Hwy 77
listings.status: Active — quiet and confirmed yours, carried deliberately rather than dropped
listings.note: ✅ THEY APPEAR HERE ON PURPOSE RATHER THAN BEING DROPPED — a listing that vanishes because nothing happened is how a seller goes ninety days without a call. ⚠️ 361 White Oak is the one real media blocker in the current marketing queue and has been flagged again this morning; the other four are covered.

pipeline.note: ⚠️ THESE NUMBERS ARE SIX DAYS OLD AND SAY SO OUT LOUD. They come from the Weekly Pipeline & Forecast of Monday 8/3 — Gene 21, account-wide 35 — and a fresh search this evening confirms no newer forecast has been issued. ⏰ THE NEXT ONE LANDS TOMORROW at 7:01 AM, so this is the last board that carries the stale figure. ⚠️ A COMPETING FIGURE OF 26 IS CIRCULATING IN THE ADVISOR LEDGER AND IT IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE — the forecast email is the system of record and it says 21. 21 at day 221 is about 6 behind an on-pace 27 and annualises to 36. ⏰ THE REAL DEADLINE IS NOT DECEMBER 31 — at 60–75 days contract-to-close, anything counting for 2026 has to be under contract by roughly October 31, now under twelve weeks. 🎉 FIELDSTONE IS THE MOVEMENT: under contract Saturday, inspection Thursday, and it closes inside 2026 on either date under discussion. ⭐ The standing target is unchanged and it is the whole game: book 3–4 real appointments this week.

money.note: ⚠️ THE MONEY SWEEP FIRED AT 6:47 THIS MORNING WITH TWO TRIGGERS AND THAT ALERT IS STILL SITTING UNREAD IN YOUR INBOX. THE SHAPE OF IT, WITHOUT NUMBERS: the fortnight's scheduled bills materially exceed the bank-stamped balance, so the account is projected short before those bills clear, and one vendor invoice came due yesterday. That is a forecast plus a due date, not a bounce. ✅ NOTHING HAS ACTUALLY FAILED — a direct sweep of the last 24 hours finds no returned item, no insufficient-funds notice and no low-balance warning. Fifth clean day on the only signal that is directly observable. 🔴 THE ONE GENUINELY SERIOUS THING IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW SIX DAYS OLD: the accounting system's cash figure is overstated by a very large multiple because its bank connection expired and was never re-linked. Every routine that has read the books for cash has been reading a number far too high — only the bank-stamped figure is usable until that link is restored. ⚠️ The benchmark file the Monday budget review runs on is still missing from this machine, so tomorrow's budget-versus-benchmark and subscription audit cannot compute until it is restored. ⭐ THE MONTH ITSELF IS NOT THE PROBLEM: August models above the survive line. September is the hole — and Fieldstone going under contract is the first real movement toward filling it.

isa.decayPolicy: ⚠️ 67 OPEN THIS EVENING, UP FROM 60 AT MIDDAY, WITH 16 AT p1 — AND EVERY p1 IS OVERDUE OR DUE TODAY. ⭐ THE LIST IS NOT ROTTING, IT IS UNATTENDED, and nearly all of tonight's growth is the machine working rather than the backlog decaying: four net-new leads were caught and correctly HELD for Monday's 7 AM queue under your Sunday no-touch rule, the CEO Sweep added the 39-address block, and one is the brand-new 821 Martinwood buyer's-agent call. 🔥 THE p1 BLOCK IS WHERE THE MONEY IS: three named buyer's agents with live interest across two listings, four named buyers off a single listing ad, a past client who replied to a reconnect in 82 minutes, and a Panama City seller who asked for a valuation in her own words. 🔴 THE NUMBER THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU IS NOT 67 — IT IS THAT THE OLDEST p1 HAS ZERO TOUCHES OF ANY KIND, SIX DAYS IN, off the exact ad that went under contract Saturday. ⚠️ THE CONTACTLESS PILE IS NOW A DECISION, NOT A QUEUE: the CEO Sweep counted 39 address-only seller submissions since 7/22 that nobody has ever called, and repeated re-pulls have returned a name, phone or email on none of them. The re-check habit is 0-for-19 and there is now a build proposal waiting on your yes to resolve owners from county records instead. ⚠️ Six inbound leads still cannot be texted at all — they typed a number carrying a do-not-call marker into your own form, and no rule exists yet for what to do with them.
isa.sweepCadence: ✅ CADENCE HELD ALL WEEKEND AND SUNDAY RAN CORRECTLY QUIET — the sweep fired on a clean half-hourly incremental from 6 AM to 5 PM and returned true zeros on every instrument, which is exactly what a Sunday should look like. Under your own no-touch rule nothing went out today; the queue is being built for Monday 7 AM. 🛑 THE SEND GATES ARE DOING WHAT YOU WROTE: cold and never-contacted leads auto-send, everyone else drafts, clients and agents get no email at all — tonight's 821 Martinwood signal went out as a CALL TASK and a private alert to you, not as mail to the buyer's agent. ⚖️ THREE QUESTIONS REPEAT EVERY RUN UNTIL YOU RULE THEM: your physical business address for cold-email footers — which has already cost one hot never-contacted Panama City seller a sent email and is now four days unanswered — whether the fleet may DRAFT a note to a co-op agent when you explicitly ask for one, which you have asked six times and been answered with a call script six times, and whether the sequence lane that follows an existing lead should stage instead of send. All three are one comment each.
